A.explanation: From $d\sin\theta = n\lambda$ with $d=1/N$, $\sin\theta = Nn\lambda$, so gradient is $Nn$.

B.explanation: This inverts the order $n$; the grating equation multiplies by $n$, giving $\sin\theta$ proportional to $n$, not $1/n$.

C.explanation: This uses slit spacing $N$ instead of $1/N$; $N$ lines per metre means $d = 1/N$, not $d = N$.

D.explanation: This is the reciprocal of the gradient; rearrangement gives $\sin\theta = Nn\lambda$, not $\lambda = Nn\sin\theta$.

hints: Notice the axes: vertical is $\sin\theta$ and horizontal is $\lambda$, so the gradient is $\sin\theta / \lambda$ for the $n$th order line through the origin.
Recall the grating equation $d\sin\theta = n\lambda$ and connect $N$ lines per metre to the slit separation using $d = 1/N$.
Rearrange to the $y = mx$ form $\sin\theta = (n/d)\lambda$ and substitute $1/d = N$ to read off the multiplier of $\lambda$.
walkthrough: Identify the graph form: $y = \sin\theta$ plotted against $x = \lambda$ is a straight line through the origin, so $\sin\theta = (\text{gradient}) \times \lambda$.
State the governing physics: for $n$th order constructive interference at a diffraction grating, $d\sin\theta = n\lambda$, where $d$ is the distance between adjacent slits.
Relate $d$ to the given $N$ lines per metre: $N$ slits occupy $1 \text{ m}$, so $d = 1/N$ in metres.
Rearrange to match the graph: $\sin\theta = (n/d)\lambda = nN\lambda$.
Compare with $y = mx$: the multiplier of $\lambda$ is $nN$, so gradient $= Nn$. This is option A.
